policy.pinning: Every community source is recorded at an exact commit and reviewed before absorption.
policy.updates: Upstream changes produce a report first; active guidance is never replaced automatically.

reviewSeverity.blocking: Wrong path or command, safety bypass, data loss risk, or false confidence
reviewSeverity.important: Materially stale, confusing, duplicated, or under-evidenced guidance
reviewSeverity.minor: Wording, naming, or organization issue without behavior change

reviewMethod.scope: Enumerated the pinned tree, read its architecture/testing material and generator, and inspected generated output.
localChecks: Generator compilation and invocation were exercised with UTF-8 console handling.
Generated output was compared with the documented module and dependency promises.

observations.statement: The source gives a coherent UDF, repository, Compose route/content, fake, and modularization foundation.
The repository identifies itself as work in progress and contains dated versions, project-specific names, and generator/documentation mismatches.
The generator's emoji console output can fail under a Windows CP1252 console unless output encoding is handled.

decision.use: Absorb architectural principles and the idea of a verified generator.
decision.exclude: Do not import pins, names, mandatory offline-first policy, or generator output without rebuilding and compiling it.

entries.nextReview: Before copying any implementation or when the upstream HEAD differs from the pinned commit.

reviewMethod.scope: Enumerated the catalog and read the router, focused skills, references, templates, and maintenance tooling.
localChecks: Catalog structure and focused skill boundaries were inspected.
Provenance and drift-detector design were compared with the Engineer governance requirements.

observations.statement: The focused-skill organization and brownfield-first routing model are a strong fit for smaller models and selective context loading.
The repository contains useful repository-boundary, coroutine ownership, debugging, and test-selection guidance.
Framework-specific recommendations and channel/flow choices are semantics-dependent and must not become universal policy.

decision.use: Adopt the router/specialist shape, provenance ledger, drift workflow, and root-cause/test discipline.
decision.exclude: Do not force a DI, networking, persistence, or testing library when the target project uses another valid stack.

entries.nextReview: Before copying any implementation or when the upstream HEAD differs from the pinned commit.

reviewMethod.scope: Read the context ladder, quick references, indexed deep references, templates, scripts, and safety/release guidance.
localChecks: All five supplied package validators passed: links, index counts, ergonomics, directive voice, and typography.
Reference indexes and the context-ladder structure were checked against the audited tree.

observations.statement: The context ladder keeps a broad production handbook usable by loading only the relevant depth.
Accessibility, localization, release, security, performance, and deterministic testing are treated as explicit gates.
Validators establish package mechanics but do not prove that every Android API claim or template compiles in combination.

decision.use: Mine production checklists, context loading, and safety boundaries into small Engineer skills.
decision.exclude: Do not activate the full handbook at once or preserve fixed platform/version opinions without current verification.

entries.nextReview: Before copying any implementation or when the upstream HEAD differs from the pinned commit.

reviewMethod.scope: Read the product-design skill and industry-conventions reference end to end.
localChecks: The workflow was compared with Android Material, adaptive-layout, and accessibility requirements.
The README licensing claim was compared with tracked files in the audited snapshot.

observations.statement: The source usefully puts user goals, task flow, states, completion, and feedback before visual polish.
Ratios, breakpoints, reading patterns, and palette conventions are heuristics, not Android requirements.
The README claims MIT licensing, but the audited snapshot has no tracked LICENSE file; copying requires clarification.

decision.use: Create original product-design routing grounded in user goals, states, Material guidance, and accessibility.
decision.exclude: Do not copy prose or present unsourced design heuristics and engagement claims as facts.

entries.nextReview: Confirm licensing and validate heuristics with design and accessibility evidence before any update.
